findings.body: The row's occurrences contain only GitHub check failures. Review findings, worker questions, run completions and readiness never produce occurrences here. New evidence beyond the RUNS deferral is that the current checkout already contains those producers: src/forge/repo.py:134–152 writes events.jsonl with fresh ids, src/forge/worker.py:224 records questions, and src/forge/review.py:495 records review results. Consequently, even a run starting and ending between refreshes remains invisible to the EVENTS consumer. Read those records, expose the applicable occurrences per item, and derive readiness identity from the review id plus head commit. Add command coverage that exercises the real producers; the current occurrence tests cover only GitHub.
findings.title: Not done: expose each item's recorded actionable occurrences

findings.body: The consumer does not match the RUNS records now present in this checkout. Tests selects step "test", but src/forge/review.py:299 writes "test run", so actual passed, failed and docs-only skipped tests all produce an empty Tests stage. Also, ended_at reads an "end" field that src/forge/repo.py:122–124 never writes, and worker.started_at reads an unproduced state field at board.py:249. Live stages therefore have no timer until their completed timing is appended. Actual run timestamps and worker models are available in events.jsonl (repo.py:137–152, worker.py:474–475 and story.py:704–705), including readers whose state has no worker family. Consume the existing producer contracts. The synthetic records in tests/test_machine_views.py:283–291 use the wrong step and invented end/running fields, so they pass while these promised behaviors are broken.
findings.title: Not done: expose recorded worker metadata and current-round stages

findings.body: The required JSON command test for a merge only a human may perform is absent. This "ready", "human" case supplies no close receipt and expects forge close, so it exercises waiting rather than a genuinely ready human-owned PR. The successful-close lifecycle test configures merge="agent" exclusively. A regression advertising forge merge for an ordinary human-owned ready PR would therefore pass these JSON tests. Close an item under human merge ownership, provide its PR, and assert through forge next --json that command is null while line describes readiness.
findings.title: Not done: command test for a human-only merge returning null

findings.body: This previously reported gap remains. Machine-board merge detection uses state files on the fetched default branch, both PR lookups request only open PRs, and the story calculation receives an empty merged-PR set here. After a human merges on GitHub but before a fetch, task and fix rows retain their previous stages and merge/close instructions. The text report already obtains merged branches in src/forge/nextstep.py:189. Reuse that evidence for machine task/fix stages and story next-step calculation.
findings.title: Recognize GitHub merges before the default branch is fetched
